newsitem.title: USA: U.S. refiners put foreign crude purchases on hold.
newsitem.headline: U.S. refiners put foreign crude purchases on hold.

text.p: U.S. refiners maintained their low profiles on Monday convinced the market was in a steady downtrend and preferred to await better bargains ahead.
Brent was nominally offered at West Texas Intermediate plus 15 cents a barrel cif for second-half November arrival, but traders said buyers were not seen.
"There are not many arbitrage opportunities. The WTI/Brent spread is not wide enough to attract U.S. refiners into the market," a Gulf Coast foreign trader said.
Dated Brent fob remained weak, with two cargoes done at December Brent minus 42 cents and 35 cents for mid November.
West African crudes like Cabinda, Bonny Light and Forcados were also noted available for late November, but interest stayed subdued on anticipation that Brent would weaken.
Regional crude markets were similarly quiet, expect for November Oriente seen available for the Gulf Coast around WTI minus $2.60-70 a barrel.
Oriente and Peruvian crude were also offered into the West Coast, but price details were sketchy, traders said.
Saudi term crude for U.S. customers were cut 5-10 cents a barrel, with Arab Light cut 10 cents, Arab Medium down five cents and Arab Heavy unchanged.
Traders said competition for outlets, including more supplies from the U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve, probably necessitated the reductions.
In the U.S. after-market, a full cargo of Dec Brent traded at $22.39 a barrel, which later changed hands at $22.40.
Partials also moved at $22.38 and $22.39, up about 15 cents from the London IPE close at $22.25.
